blocks.text: First-row transition elements show variable oxidation states because the 3d and 4s subshells have very similar energies. Like the 4s electrons, the 3d electrons can also be lost easily, so both take part in bonding. A 3d metal atom can lose only its 4s electrons, usually giving the common +2 state, or the 4s electrons together with some 3d electrons, giving higher states. Manganese reaches the highest, +7. Across the row the maximum oxidation state rises to manganese and then falls (a parabolic trend).
